description: One irrigation zone inside a field: where the water comes from, which water right it runs under, how much of it there is and what puts it on the ground. The zone is the unit a valve turns, which makes it the smallest unit water cost and water quality can honestly be attributed to.

fields.description: What the zone is called at the valve: 'YC3-Zone2'. The docname is built from this and the parcel's abbreviation — not the field's, because the zone name already carries its field and 'YC3-Zone2 - YC3' says nothing twice.
fields.label: Zone Name

fields.description: The block this zone waters.
fields.label: Field

fields.description: The parcel the field is on. Copied from the field, and the key the docname is suffixed with.
fields.label: Parcel

fields.description: The zone's number within its field, as the controller has it. Two zones of one field cannot share a number: that number is what somebody types into the irrigation controller at two in the morning.
fields.label: Zone Number

fields.description: Irrigated area in square feet, which is the unit a design drawing uses.
fields.label: Area (sq ft)

fields.description: The same area in acres, computed from square feet at 43,560 to the acre. Stored rather than derived at read time so a report can sort on it; recomputed on every save, so it cannot drift from the square footage.
fields.label: Area (acres)

fields.description: Where the water comes from. This is the first question in an FSMA agricultural water assessment and the first question in a drought year, which is the same question.
fields.label: Water Source
fields.options:
well
creek
municipal
pond
shared
other

fields.description: The Oregon water right or certificate number this zone draws under. Without it a surface-water zone is a zone nobody can prove the right to run.
fields.label: Water Right ID

fields.description: Design flow in gallons per minute. With area this gives application rate, which is what a set length is calculated from.
fields.label: Flow Rate (GPM)

fields.description: What puts the water on the ground. Drip and micro wet the soil; impact and gun wet the fruit, which is what makes them an agricultural-water question rather than only an agronomic one.
fields.label: Sprinkler Type

fields.description: Agricultural water compliance for this zone. It is here rather than in a compliance register because the zone is the unit the water actually moves through: a test result that is not attached to a valve cannot tell anybody which fruit to hold.
fields.label: Agricultural Water Compliance

fields.description: When this zone's water was last tested. FSMA Produce Safety Rule Subpart E sets the testing cadence; the operational use is the same date — an untested zone on a block that overhead-irrigates ready-to-eat fruit is a zone you do not run before harvest.
fields.label: Water Test Last Date

fields.description: The water quality class this source is assessed at, I through IV. Class drives the testing cadence and whether the water may contact harvestable fruit at all.
fields.label: Water Source Class

fields.description: Ticked when this zone is running a chlorination or other antimicrobial treatment. It changes what a test result means and it changes what the crew handles at the pump house, which is why it lives with the zone.
fields.label: Chlorination Active

fields.description: The shape on the ground. Everything below the polygon is DERIVED from it on save and must not be edited by hand — a figure a person can change independently of the polygon is a figure that will disagree with it, and the disagreement surfaces as a geofence saying no to somebody standing in the right place.
fields.label: Boundary

fields.description: The zone boundary as a GeoJSON Polygon or MultiPolygon, in [longitude, latitude] degrees. Set it with the boundary tool rather than by hand: they validate the shape and recompute everything derived from it. A zone is expected to sit inside its block's boundary; one that does not is reported rather than refused.
fields.label: Boundary (GeoJSON)

fields.description: Computed. Where a map opens, and the cheap first cut for a distance query. For a shape whose true centroid falls outside it — a block wrapped round a farmstead — this is an interior point instead, because centring on the farmstead is centring on somebody else's ground.
fields.label: Centroid Latitude

fields.description: Computed. See Centroid Latitude.
fields.label: Centroid Longitude

fields.description: Computed. A bounding box is a guaranteed superset of the shape it bounds, which is what makes it the only safe cheap prefilter for 'is this point inside' — a candidate set built from it can never miss the right answer.
fields.label: Bounding Box (GeoJSON)

fields.description: Computed. JSON of {resolution: [cells]} at resolutions 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10, holding every cell the shape TOUCHES. Not every cell whose centre is inside it: an orchard block is smaller than one cell at resolutions 6 to 8, so a centre-based fill returns nothing for most fields and an index built on it would answer 'in no field' for a point plainly in one.
fields.label: H3 Cells

fields.description: Computed from the polygon by spherical excess. This is a different number from the acreage somebody typed and both are worth having: a deed, a GIS trace and a tape measure routinely disagree by a few percent. A gap over 5% is reported; over 25% the boundary is refused, because at that point one of the two figures is about a different piece of ground.
fields.label: Computed Area (acres)
Schedule
fields.description: v0.248.0. The zone's planned sets. Raised as Irrigation tasks each day when Irrigation Schedule is on in ERPNext MCP Settings.

name: Irrigation Zone
